headline: High risk: Langflow’s default server-side, unsandboxed flow execution can amplify Caveman outputs into unsafe actions and data exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Caveman can use MCP and writes/reads project files like CLAUDE.md, while Langflow chains multiple agents and wires tools into flow nodes. That creates a plausible instruction-bridging path if Caveman content is fed into Langflow flows, though no shared channel is documented by default. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Caveman output is copied into a Langflow prompt or node input
IF a Langflow flow treats file content or upstream text as instructions
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation prompt
Disable automatic ingestion of upstream text into agent prompts
Review one representative flow for prompt-injection handling
Use a human approval step before executing chained agent outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Langflow reads and writes server filesystem files and stores per-flow credentials. Langflow’s broad network egress and arbitrary HTTP components make leakage to third parties plausible if Caveman-managed content is routed into flows. This is a default-dangerous pairing unless deployment isolation is strong.
conditions: IF Caveman project notes or memory files are loaded into Langflow flows
IF Langflow components send flow inputs to external model providers or HTTP services
mitigations: Keep Caveman files out of Langflow workspaces
Rotate any credentials stored in Langflow if shared inputs were used
Restrict Langflow components to local-only providers
Audit one flow for outbound HTTP and file-read steps
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents on separate storage and principals

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Caveman supports multiple instances and uses files/MCP, while Langflow supports multiple instances, server-side shared state, and unrestricted filesystem write. Both can mutate overlapping workspace artifacts, so concurrent runs can overwrite or race on shared files even though Langflow does not modify git state. The shared-state design makes conflict likely in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or server-side store
IF Caveman writes project notes while Langflow writes uploaded files or intermediate outputs
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Disable concurrent runs on the same workspace
Review one shared path for overlapping writes
requires-engineering: add per-agent storage isolation

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow’s graph-based flows can chain multiple agents and tools, so Caveman-generated text can become authoritative input to downstream actions without a built-in verification step. Caveman is a content-writing agent, which increases the chance that its outputs are treated as facts or instructions. The pair therefore supports error amplification into external actions or generated artifacts.
conditions: IF a Langflow flow routes Caveman output directly into another agent or tool node
IF downstream nodes execute shell commands or external API calls based on that output
mitigations: Insert a validation node between Caveman and action nodes
Require human review before any tool-executing branch
Constrain downstream nodes to read-only transforms
Test one flow with a deliberately wrong Caveman output
requires-engineering: add schema checks for all inter-node messages

E_compliance.rationale: Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and intermediate outputs on a server filesystem. That creates a retention and residency mismatch risk if the same regulated data class is routed through both systems. No specific jurisdictional mismatch is documented, so this is a policy-gap rather than a breach by default.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Caveman memory files or project notes
IF Langflow retains the same data in flow stores or server files beyond the intended retention window
mitigations: Classify one sample data flow and check retention settings
Delete any test secrets from Langflow stores
Keep regulated data out of shared flow inputs
Document a retention owner for both systems
requires-engineering: align deletion/export workflows across both agents
